in: Section 1: scope and authority -- what this brief is for, that it authorizes nothing, and the exact boundary 13F section 6 draws for Palo Alto (three method classes: direct-firewall API reads, Panorama target=<serial> reads, and Panorama's own configuration read; no commit, no push, no write of any class; no direct SSH to a firewall, per PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_13C SB-11's measured reasoning).

Section 2: the question set, each phrased so the answer is observed behaviour rather than opinion. At minimum: (a) how a session key is obtained and how long it is valid, and whether the key can be sent only in a header; (b) which route returns the identity facts (serial, hostname, model, software version, HA state) and which element names carry them; (c) which route enumerates interfaces WITH every address on them, and how a high-availability floating address is distinguished from an interface's own address; (d) which route returns the routing table, and whether it is paginated or truncated on a large table; (e) what effective-running returns, how large it is, and how it differs from the active configuration and from merged -- asked as three separate questions, not assumed equivalent; (f) whether a virtual-system-scoped read exists for each of (c) to (e) and how the virtual system is selected; (g) which reads are available through Panorama with target=<serial> and whether the response differs in shape from the same read taken directly; (h) what Panorama's own configuration read returns for Template, Template Stack and Device Group assignment, and under which element paths; (i) whether any response can carry a credential, key or other secret; (j) what a failure looks like -- HTTP status, an error element, or a success envelope carrying an error.

Section 3: the exact request list the Product Owner runs, ordered and numbered, each shown as a runnable form with placeholders for estate values, each annotated with the question it answers and with 'read-only, class 0' or a stop. Credentials are shown only in a POST body or a header form, never in a URL, and the brief says why in one line. For each request, what to RECORD: element names and their nesting paths, response shape, counts, sizes -- counts and shapes only, per AGENTS.md sensitive identity reporting law, with an explicit reminder at the top of the section that no address, hostname, serial or configuration content is to be pasted back.

Section 4: what must be recorded about the configuration reads specifically, because 13F section 3 requires one read and two outputs: the size of effective-running on a typical device, whether two consecutive reads of an unchanged device are byte-identical (the digest question), and which element categories would have to be removed for the sanitized view copy -- described by category, never by example.

Section 5: the Panorama-side questions kept separate from the direct-firewall ones, because 13F section 1 gives them different evidence roles: what target=<serial> reads are for, what Panorama's own configuration read is for, and the explicit question of whether a fact appearing in both planes ever disagrees -- and what the Product Owner should record when it does.

Section 6: what the brief deliberately does NOT ask, with the reason -- no commit, push or write of any class; no backup command (C7 owns that); no failover or HA state change; no direct SSH to a firewall; no Check Point question; and no request whose purpose is to test reachability rather than to read a fact.

Section 7: the acceptance shape of the answer -- what a complete measurement record looks like, mirroring the Check Point handover's structure (method table, request forms, element-binding table, open verification items), so the follow-on findings document and the collection contract have a fixed target.

Add one backlog item for the follow-on work (the Palo Alto collection contract, blocked on this measurement) through scripts/project_queue.py -- never hand-edit project/*.json. Do not touch CURRENT_STATE.md. Commit early and often.

Running any request anywhere; contacting any firewall or Panorama.
Check Point in any form; backup and restore routes (C7); any write of any class; any commit, push or policy operation; any direct SSH to a firewall.
Editing any FROZEN document, or applying a status to any document.
Closing or changing any of the discovery transport's 18 UNVERIFIED element bindings -- a different measurement, already briefed separately.
Any address, hostname, serial, certificate subject or configuration content anywhere in the document.

Section 2 asks 16 numbered questions (Q-1..Q-16): session-key acquisition and validity/header-only transport; failure shape; identity route and element names; interface enumeration with every address and HA-floating-address distinction; routing-table route and truncation/pagination behaviour; effective-running, active configuration and merged asked as three separate questions; virtual-system-scoped reads for each of interfaces/routes/configuration, asked per route rather than assumed; Panorama target=<serial> availability and shape-parity per route; Panorama's own configuration read for Template/Template Stack/Device Group provenance; cross-plane disagreement; secret-carrying responses; two-read digest stability of effective-running.

Section 3 lists 19 ordered, numbered, runnable requests (R-1..R-19), each annotated with the question it answers and 'read-only, class 0'; credentials shown only in a POST body or an X-PAN-KEY header, never a URL, with the one-line reason (PAN_AUTH_TRANSPORT_CONVERGENCE_AUDIT.md's urgent finding); each request states what to RECORD as element names/paths/shapes/counts/sizes only, with an explicit no-paste-back reminder at the top of the section.

Section 4 records what the configuration-retention questions (13F CF-1/CF-2) require: effective-running size, the two-read byte-identity/digest question (R-7 run twice), and configuration categories to remove for the sanitized view copy, by category only.

Section 5 separates the Panorama-side questions from the direct-firewall ones per 13F section 1's distinct evidence roles, and asks explicitly whether a fact appearing on both planes ever disagrees, with MATCH/MISMATCH/NOT_EVALUABLE as the only recordable outcomes.

Section 6 states what the brief deliberately does not ask and why: no write of any class, no backup command (C7 owns that), no failover/HA change, no direct SSH to a firewall (13C SB-11's measured reason), no Check Point question, no bare-reachability probe.

Section 7 fixes the acceptance shape of the follow-on findings document (method table, request forms actually used, element-binding table, Q-16 digest finding, cross-plane comparison table, open-verification-items list), mirroring the Check Point handover and the PAN discovery findings document.
Section 8 cross-references every authority cited, all verified to exist at HEAD before citing.
